title: Yuma Regional Medical Center to pay $1,985,000 to settle 2022 ransomware data breach lawsuit
date_note: HIPAA Journal's publication day; the settlement is reported on that day. The attack itself was April 21-25, 2022.
summary: HIPAA Journal reports a $1,985,000 settlement fund in the class action Dillon Clarke, et al. v. Yuma Regional Medical Center (D. Arizona) over a ransomware attack in which hackers accessed systems between April 21 and April 25, 2022. 738,145 individuals were reported to HHS OCR; names, Social Security numbers, health insurance and limited medical information were involved. The center denies the claims and wrongdoing.
plain: A hospital in Arizona agreed to a $1,985,000 settlement of a lawsuit over a 2022 ransomware attack that exposed data of 738,145 people, according to a news report.
exec: Data breach litigation can cost millions years after an attack, even when the organisation denies liability.
action: No action needed; for awareness. Affected patients should check the settlement notice for claim deadlines.
impact: 738,145 individuals reported to HHS OCR; individual reimbursement capped at $4,000 for documented losses, plus one year of medical data monitoring.
